cf.title: BUG #19772: ERROR: corrupt MVNDistinct entry for GROUP BY c0, ROLLUP (abs(c0)) with ndistinct statistics

input.subject: BUG #19772: ERROR: corrupt MVNDistinct entry for GROUP BY c0, ROLLUP (abs(c0)) with ndistinct statistics

verdict_reasoning: The patch fixes a plan-time error on valid SQL and extends the nullingrels stripping that e28033fe1 already added to selfuncs.c. The one surviving objection, maintenance-fit-1, is fixable: the back-patch to v18 also changes estimates for queries that run today, and the thread shows no test or comparison for that. A committer who knows the planner has to decide the scope of the back-patch.

brief.title: Strip GROUP RTE nullingrels in selfuncs.c to fix corrupt MVNDistinct entry
brief.problem: With an ndistinct extended statistics object, a query like GROUP BY c0, ROLLUP (abs(c0)) fails at plan time with "corrupt MVNDistinct entry". It affects users of extended statistics on v18, v19rc1 and master; the reporter says 14.24 runs the same queries without error. A query fuzzer found it.
brief.proposed_design: Since f5050f795, Vars inside a grouping expression missing from some grouping sets carry the GROUP RTE index in their nullingrels. The patch strips that index wherever selfuncs.c already strips outer-join nullingrels before looking up statistics, so estimate_num_groups no longer counts the same column twice. It is back-patched to v18.
author_claims: The GROUP RTE bit makes estimate_num_groups add two GroupVarInfos for one column, and estimate_multivariate_ndistinct then reports the error.
The same bit kept examine_variable from matching such expressions to expression indexes or extended statistics expressions.
e28033fe1 fixed the same error for outer-join nullingrels.
The fix belongs in v18 and later, where the GROUP RTE was introduced.
brief.thread_state: The bug report and one reply with a v1 patch are visible. The author CCed Richard, who wrote f5050f795 and e28033fe1, but nobody else has replied.
unclear: The material does not say whether stripping the GROUP RTE index changes group-count or selectivity estimates for queries that did not error before.
The patch says expression-index and extended-statistics matching also improves, but the material does not say whether tests cover it.
The material does not say whether code outside selfuncs.c compares Vars in a way that hits the same GROUP RTE nullingrels issue.
The material does not say which reported query variants the new stats_ext regression tests cover.

objections.title: Back-patch changes estimates for queries that did not error
objections.failure_scenario: A v18 user runs grouping sets over an expression that has an expression index or extended statistics expression, with no error today. After the minor update, examine_variable matches that statistic, the group estimate changes, and the plan flips. The user finds out from a slower query in production after the upgrade.
objections.argument: The commit message names two effects: the fix for the "corrupt MVNDistinct entry" error, and new matching of expression indexes and extended statistics expressions. Only the first is the reported bug in message #1. The second changes estimates for working queries in a stable branch, and the material shows no test or measurement of it. Stripping the GROUP RTE bit everywhere outer-join bits are stripped does follow existing practice from e28033fe1, so the master change itself is fair.
objections.author_must_show: Is the estimate change for queries that do not error intended for v18 back-branches, or can the back-patch be limited to the duplicate-GroupVarInfo fix?

critic.reasoning: The commit message itself names the new expression-index and extended-statistics matching, and the material shows no test or estimate comparison for it. The change probably restores pre-v18 matching, since the GROUP RTE bit did not exist then, but the thread does not say so.

touch_points.label: planner behaviour change
touch_points.reason: Stripping the GROUP RTE index in selfuncs.c changes group-count estimates and lets examine_variable match expression indexes and extended statistics expressions.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The commit message asks for a back-patch to v18, where estimates for queries that run today may change.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Is the estimate change for queries that do not error today intended for the v18 back-branch, or can the back-patch be limited to the duplicate-GroupVarInfo fix?
Does stripping the GROUP RTE index restore the pre-v18 matching of expression indexes and extended statistics expressions, and can a before-and-after estimate show it?
Which of the query variants in message #1 do the new stats_ext tests cover, and does any test cover the expression-index matching?
Does any code outside selfuncs.c compare Vars for a statistics lookup in a way that the GROUP RTE index in nullingrels also breaks?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows planner selectivity estimation and the GROUP RTE nullingrels handling; the author CCed the author of f5050f795 and e28033fe1, who has not replied.
committability.liability: Plan changes in v18 minor releases for grouping-sets queries over expressions, and correct stripping at every statistics lookup site in selfuncs.c, for the life of the v18 branch and later.
committability.author_follow_up: The author answered the report within two days with an analysis and a patch and created the CommitFest entry; no later sign either way.

priority.reason: The error needs an ndistinct statistics object and grouping sets over an expression of a grouped column, but it is a regression since v18 on valid SQL. The patch is 7.1 KB, touches selfuncs.c and stats_ext tests, and follows the pattern of e28033fe1.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so it is unknown whether the patch strips the GROUP RTE index at every lookup site in selfuncs.c and only there. The size of the estimate change for queries that run today could not be judged.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: estimating joins using extended statistics
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch uses multi-column MCV lists from extended statistics to estimate equijoin selectivity, matching the MCV lists of the two joined relations the way eqjoinsel_inner does. It can also use base restrictions as conditions on the MCV lists, and estimates joins of more than two relations one relation pair at a time.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No reviewer objected to the design in the visible messages. The last messages report that the 2022-01-01 version fails cfbot with uninitialized-variable warnings in mcv_combine_simple() and no longer applies to master, and no new version appears before the entry was returned. The author still listed open items, such as no support for outer or inequality joins and possibly wrong ndistinct and nullfract assumptions for column subsets.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Also the patch doesn't apply anymore:

precedents_retrieved.title: Parallel grouping sets
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add parallel execution of GROUPING SETS queries by splitting aggregation into partial and final stages, first by grouping on the union of all grouping columns in workers and doing the grouping-sets aggregation in the leader. The later version instead performs grouping-sets aggregation in workers, tags each partial tuple with a grouping set ID, and has the leader combine results per grouping set, with refactoring of nodeAgg.c (phase reorganisation, sorting inside the Agg node).
precedents_retrieved.objection: The last patch version received no review and no longer applied to HEAD. A PGCon hallway-track discussion of the approach concluded that nodeAgg.c needs refactoring before it is complicated further, and after an off-list discussion with Melanie, who had picked up the patch, the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
There was also considerable discussion in a (virtual) hallway-track session
during PGCon which reviewed the approach (for lack of a better description),
deeming that nodeAgg.c needs a refactoring before complicating it further.

precedents_retrieved.title: Skip a redundant singleton GROUP BY node
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch series lets the planner skip a plain GROUP BY step, adding projection paths in place of aggregate paths, when a unique index on a single base or partitioned table proves each input row is its own group. Patch 1 moves the unique-index matching logic out of remove_useless_groupby_columns() into a shared helper.
precedents_retrieved.objection: David Rowley noted that this was the author's third new thread on the topic in about three weeks, and that the idea is proposed regularly on the list. He also pointed to earlier discussions and to a patch for the same thing already in the commitfest, and advised against pursuing this one. The author agreed to review those proposals and the existing patch; the entry was then withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
For this one, I wouldn't bother as the idea gets proposed regularly on
this mailing list.

precedents_retrieved.title: remove_useless_groupby_columns is too enthusiastic
precedents_retrieved.summary: Change remove_useless_groupby_columns so that it no longer removes GROUP BY items that are functionally dependent on a primary key when those items also appear in ORDER BY. This keeps the link between the GROUP BY and ORDER BY lists, so the planner can use a sorted index path with GroupAggregate and avoid an explicit sort.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers pointed out that keeping the redundant columns can make plans worse. Without a matching index, the extra sort columns cost more (Richard Guo measured a slowdown). Hash Aggregate would always pay for hashing and comparing the extra columns. David Rowley proposed a different design: mark redundant GROUP BY columns instead of removing them, and consider both the full and the minimal key sets. No revised patch followed, and the entry was marked Returned with Feedback after the thread had been idle for some weeks following that review.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So the
patch makes that case worse in favour of possibly making Group
Aggregate cases better.

precedents_retrieved.title: group locking
precedents_retrieved.summary: Robert Haas proposed a heavyweight-lock concept of "locking groups" for parallelism: a user backend and its worker backends would form a group whose lock requests never conflict with each other, with changes to lock acquisition, wait-queue handling and the deadlock detector so that no group member waits behind an unrelated process. The posted patch was an incomplete draft (LockAcquireExtended() and ProcSleep() modified, ProcWakeup() and the deadlock detector not) meant to get feedback on the design.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the leader could hold the locks for its workers, and that the proposal added too much complexity, with bugs and performance costs, to the lock manager. Andres Freund objected that letting group members hold self-exclusive locks at the same time removes guarantees that existing code relies on, citing transaction abort (smgrDoPendingDeletes) and relcache invalidation. Robert Haas then dropped the original design because it would put too much coordination burden on the workers, and moved to granting the leader's existing locks to workers at the start of a parallel operation. The visible thread ends without agreement on that alternative or a revised patch, and the closing decision is not shown.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Based on your arguments and those of others, I have long-since abandoned the original proposal of having locks within a group never conflict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Extended statistics / estimate Var op Var clauses
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch series lets the planner use extended statistics (MCV lists) to estimate (Var op Var) clauses such as a < b, which before were estimated only for (Var op Const). It also improves selfuncs estimates for clauses with the same expression on both sides, such as a = a, and changes which clauses count as "simple" in the MCV OR handling.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Dean Rasheed's July 2022 review found that the change to "issimple" handling makes some estimates worse, for example WHERE a = 1 OR (b > 0 AND b < 10), and no existing regression test caught this. He asked whether that part was still needed after the selfuncs fixes. The author did not answer for two months, so Michael Paquier marked the entry Returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The patch changes that, which ends up making things worse in some cases.

precedents_retrieved.title: rewriteGraphTable: Fix missing RTEs in FROM clause by setting inFromCl=true
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch sets inFromCl = true on the range table entries that rewriteGraphTable creates for GRAPH_TABLE queries, so that deparsed queries list those relations in the FROM clause. The author wanted this so extensions such as pg_pgq2sql and pg_duckdb can get runnable SQL for graph queries through pg_get_querydef.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. A quoted reply from Ashutosh notes that the subquery RTEs added for views during rewriting have inFromCl = false and suggests a second solution, which the author answered with a use-case argument and a UNION test. The entry was later withdrawn, and the thread shows no decision.

precedents_retrieved.title: (SQL/PGQ) cache lookup failed for label
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes dependency.c record dependencies on the property graph labels and properties (GraphLabelRef and GraphPropertyRef nodes) that a GRAPH_TABLE view uses. Dropping a label or property that a view still uses then fails with a dependency error, where before the view later failed with "cache lookup failed for label".
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The original author said he had no time to address review comments, and Ayush Tiwari then posted v2 and v3 with tests; no one objected to the approach before the entry was withdrawn the same day.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert applying column aliases to the output of whole-row Vars.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert applying column aliases to the output of whole-row Vars.
Reverted commit(s): Ensure that RowExprs and whole-row Vars produce the expected column names.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
In commit bf7ca1587, I had the bright idea that we could make the
result of a whole-row Var (that is, foo.*) track any column aliases
that had been applied to the FROM entry the Var refers to.  However,
that's not terribly logically consistent, because now the output of
the Var is no longer of the named composite type that the Var claims
to emit.  bf7ca1587 tried to handle that by changing the output
tuple values to be labeled with a blessed RECORD type, but that's
really pretty disastrous: we can wind up storing such tuples onto
disk, whereupon they're not readable by other sessions.

The only practical fix I can see is to give up on what bf7ca1587
tried to do, and say that the column names of tuples produced by
a whole-row Var are always those of the underlying named composite
type, query aliases or no.  While this introduces some inconsistencies,
it removes others, so it's not that awful in the abstract.  What *is*
kind of awful is to make such a behavioral change in a back-patched
bug fix.  But corrupt data is worse, so back-patched it will be.

(A workaround available to anyone who's unhappy about this is to
introduce an extra level of sub-SELECT, so that the whole-row Var is
referring to the sub-SELECT's output and not to a named table type.
Then the Var is of type RECORD to begin with and there's no issue.)

Per report from Miles Delahunty.  The faulty commit dates to 9.5,
so back-patch to all supported branches.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Optimize order of GROUP BY keys".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Optimize order of GROUP BY keys".
Reverted commit(s): Optimize order of GROUP BY keys
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit db0d67db2401eb6238ccc04c6407a4fd4f985832 and
several follow-on fixes.  The idea of making a cost-based choice
of the order of the sorting columns is not fundamentally unsound,
but it requires cost information and data statistics that we don't
really have.  For example, relying on procost to distinguish the
relative costs of different sort comparators is pretty pointless
so long as most such comparator functions are labeled with cost 1.0.
Moreover, estimating the number of comparisons done by Quicksort
requires more than just an estimate of the number of distinct values
in the input: you also need some idea of the sizes of the larger
groups, if you want an estimate that's good to better than a factor of
three or so.  That's data that's often unknown or not very reliable.
Worse, to arrive at estimates of the number of calls made to the
lower-order-column comparison functions, the code needs to make
estimates of the numbers of distinct values of multiple columns,
which are necessarily even less trustworthy than per-column stats.
Even if all the inputs are perfectly reliable, the cost algorithm
as-implemented cannot offer useful information about how to order
sorting columns beyond the point at which the average group size
is estimated to drop to 1.

Close inspection of the code added by db0d67db2 shows that there
are also multiple small bugs.  These could have been fixed, but
there's not much point if we don't trust the estimates to be
accurate in-principle.

Finally, the changes in cost_sort's behavior made for very large
changes (often a factor of 2 or so) in the cost estimates for all
sorting operations, not only those for multi-column GROUP BY.
That naturally changes plan choices in many situations, and there's
precious little evidence to show that the changes are for the better.
Given the above doubts about whether the new estimates are really
trustworthy, it's hard to summon much confidence that these changes
are better on the average.

Since we're hard up against the release deadline for v15, let's
revert these changes for now.  We can always try again later.

Note: in v15, I left T_PathKeyInfo in place in nodes.h even though
it's unreferenced.  Removing it would be an ABI break, and it seems
a bit late in the release cycle for that.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the precedent list has no earlier attempt at this idea. Message #2 points to e28033fe1 as a fix of the same error for outer-join nullingrels, and this patch extends that approach to the GROUP RTE, so no earlier rejection reason applies.

The patch changes no SQL syntax, GUC, catalog, dump output or psql behaviour, so the user-facing contract is untouched. Back-patching may change group-count and expression-statistics estimates in 18.x, but it moves them back toward pre-v18 behaviour, before the GROUP RTE existed. That makes it a weak case for a plan-stability objection.

The fix changes only planner estimation in selfuncs.c and adds regression tests. It touches no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog, wire protocol message, or exported struct, so it has no persistent or cross-node state to object to. Back-patching to 18 carries no pg_upgrade or ABI risk that the commit message shows, although the code was not visible to confirm that no function signature changes.

The patch changes only how selfuncs.c compares Vars before it looks up statistics for planner estimates. It adds no privilege, role, setting or user-visible surface, so no new data becomes visible to any user. Better matching to expression indexes and extended statistics still goes through the existing statistics permission and leakproof checks in examine_variable, and the patch does not appear to change those checks. Whether that holds in the code could not be checked here.
The master-branch design extends an existing pattern in selfuncs.c and adds no hot-path cost or new API. The author of the related commits is CCed but has not replied yet.

This is a bug fix for a planner error. No existing feature, extension or setting avoids it short of dropping the ndistinct statistics object. The patch extends the existing nullingrels stripping in selfuncs.c and adds no second mechanism, so this angle has nothing to raise.

This is a bug fix for a plan-time ERROR on valid SQL, a regression since v18 that 14.24 does not have. A fuzzer finding it does not weaken demand: any user with ndistinct statistics who writes such a grouping-sets query gets an error. Costs stay inside selfuncs.c statistics lookup, with no new user-visible surface.
